rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: status (request bytes the backend read: 65) expected:<502> but was:<200> at ProxyTlsTest.lp14r2_1_hostNameCheckStaysOnWithAChainOnlyExtendedTrustManager(ProxyTlsTest.java:666)
rows.note: A private-CA .sslSocketFactory whose trust manager is an X509ExtendedTrustManager that checks the chain (delegating to the PKIX manager's two-argument checkServerTrusted) but not the endpoint: the JDK does not wrap an X509ExtendedTrustManager, so setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS") reads back but checks nothing, and TlsConnector skips its HostnameVerifier off Android (verifyAfterIdentification=false). The other.example certificate reaches the backend for target localhost: host name verification is off with the option, against PRD-165.

rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: status (errors: [com.snoworca.naruserve.proxy.ProxyException]) expected:<200> but was:<502> at ProxyTlsTest.lp14r2_2_aDelegatingPrivateCaFactoryReachesTheGoodBackend(ProxyTlsTest.java:681)
rows.note: Fail-closed side of the 32cda82 fix: with the AC-8 DelegatingFactory (base get/setSSLParameters) over the private-CA context, the identification does not read back, so TlsConnector falls to HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier(), which rejects every host on the JDK. A correct certificate for localhost therefore never reaches the backend on a JVM; every delegating private-CA factory is unusable there.

rows.note: Variant of r1 LP-2 that defeats the read-back of 32cda82: a delegating SSLSocket that keeps the SSLParameters it was given (so getSSLParameters reads back "HTTPS") while the base setSSLParameters applies only protocols/cipher suites to the real socket. Host name verification ends up off with no option. Root cause shared with LP-1/LP-3: on the JDK the proxy never checks the session's peer certificate against the host itself.
